messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike observed for /v1/generate (hosted, us-west1). Impact: elevated error-free tail latency. Paging on-call SRE. Auto-run: collect-traces, snapshot-profiles.

alex: paging @infra-sre and @maria — looks like customer traffic spike + big p95 jump ~08:12. Are we seeing backend queuing?

maria: got the page, joining. quick summary: p50 ~90ms -> 95ms, p95 jumped 400ms -> 1.4s around 08:12 UTC. Error rate unchanged.

srinivas: grabbing traces now. initial flamegraphs show long kernel syscalls on socket recvfrom at tail spans. attaching first trace id: trace-0a3f9 (link: https://a.pm/trace/0a3f9)

emily: oncall handoff: I'm taking lead for mitigation. alex — can you open an incident ticket with customer impact note? I pinged support to flag top customers in us-west.

alex: incident created: INC-2026-1427. Customer-impact note: interactive features may see degraded reply times 1-2s for a subset of requests. Support notified.

maria: quick mitigation idea: widen routing to us-west2 for non-data-resident customers, and enable model-fallback to smaller variant (gptx-4-lite) for requests above 1024 tokens. Can do a conservative rollout. Thoughts?

infra-sre: before routing, let's check kernel patch rollouts — we had a kernel micro-patch deployed to node-pool-2 at 07:50. I'll list nodes patched vs unpatched. Running: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=nodepool=nlp-pool-2"` and `kubectl get pods -o wide`

kevin: logs from a patched host: ```Mar 05 07:53:12 host kernel: tcp_sock_read_iter+0x1a4 slowpath at 0xffffffff
dmesg excerpt: watch for high softirq latencies
perf record shows sys_read and futex_wait appearing in top stacks```

srinivas: traces correlate: requests that hit a patched host show tail spans stuck on `epoll_wait` -> then long kernel scheduling wakeups. Unpatched hosts show normal spans. hypothesis: regressed kernel path for epoll/softirq handling.

emily: mitigation plan: 1) cordon patched hosts in nlp-pool-2 and redirect traffic away, 2) rollback kernel patch on pool nodes, 3) temporarily enable model-fallback + route to us-west2. I can run (1) immediately.

maria: executing cordon/evict now: `kubectl cordon node-017` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets node-017` — repeating across 6 nodes. Starting with node-017, node-019, node-023. Monitoring load balancer health.

alex: support update: two customers reported UI slowness; both on us-west1. Not yet a full outage but escalating to enterprise success teams.

infra-sre: evidence: `perf top` on node-017 shows heavy cycles in `ep_poll_wait` and `__do_softirq`. Also network irq delays visible in /proc/interrupts. Patch ID: kp-2026-03-05-epoll. I'll open a rollback CL.

srinivas: collecting traces for post-cordon traffic: new traces routed to unpatched nodes show p95 back to ~210ms within 3m of cordon. attaching short trace summary: `p95-before=1400ms p95-after=210ms p50-before=95ms p50-after=88ms`

emily: good. executing rollback now on a small batch, then will coordinate full rollback with infra-sre. Will keep canary for 10m then full.

kevin: adding perf counters we pulled earlier: `softirq_total: +320%`, `context_switches: +18%`, `net_rx_packets_dropped: +0.2%` — may indicate scheduling/backpressure in net stack.

maria: running a quick BPF to capture epoll latency distribution: `bpftool` script saved to s3://rdw-ops/epoll-bpf/1976543210.log (link).

infra-sre: rollback CL merged and applied to pool-2 canary nodes at 08:25. Observed immediate reduction in softirq and epoll busy loops. Rolling to remaining nodes now.

alex: updating INC-2026-1427 with timeline and mitigation steps. Noted that rollback restored p95 to baseline for most traffic.

srinivas: tracking follow-ups: 1) kernel regression root cause (compare commit diffs), 2) add load-aware early drain when softirq spikes, 3) add synthetic tail-latency monitors per node. I'll start a timeline doc.

emily: final status for now: mitigated — traffic rebalanced, rollback applied, p95 almost recovered. Keeping incident open for RCA work and customer follow-up. Paging out to platform and kernel teams for deep dive. :white_check_mark:
